2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.the_problem: a count cannot prove completeness against itself. 15 rows are 15 rows whether or not a 16th game existed, so trusting the board's own expected_game_count=15 would be circular.
2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.the_invariant_used: MLB has 30 franchises. On a full single-header slate each appears in exactly one game. 15 games in which all 30 KNOWN franchise abbreviations appear exactly once is complete BY CONSTRUCTION: a 16th game would repeat a franchise, and a missing game would leave two absent.
2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.result_2026_08_15: COMPLETE_BY_INVARIANT — 15 canonical tier-1 finals, 30/30 franchises, max appearances 1

2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.independent_second_confirmation: the diff module's selftest asserts every team gains EXACTLY 2 games between the pre-refresh and post-refresh form states. It passes for all 20 slate teams — which is only possible if both dates were full 15-game slates. Two unrelated code paths agree.
2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.a_hole_this_closed_in_my_own_gate: the invariant first counted DISTINCT NAMES, so a typo ('NY Yankees') would have read as a 30th franchise while a real one was absent, and the slate would have passed. Its own selftest caught this before it was ever run on live data; the check is now set membership against the frozen 30 abbreviations, with a dedicated typo fixture.
2_COMPLETENESS_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN.not_asserted: on a partial slate the invariant genuinely cannot distinguish an off-day from a missing game. Such a date is reported UNVERIFIABLE_BY_INVARIANT_PARTIAL_SLATE with the absent franchises named — never as complete.
